Fit MOSK GP to 2-band synthetic example

This notebook contains the workflow for:

  • loading groundtruth 2-band (MOGP) time-series,
  • fitting a MOSK GP model,
  • drawing posterior predictive samples,
  • visualising the posteriors .
library(here)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(cmdstanr)
library(posterior)
library(bayesplot)
library(readr)
library(glue)
library(tictoc)

register_knitr_engine(override = FALSE)

theme_set(theme_bw())
color_scheme_set("viridis") # bayesplot

source(here("mogp-utils.R"))

filename_stub <- "D2-Q1-seed2495-n300-mnar0.3-noise0.05"

EXECUTE_SAMPLING <- FALSE
# SAMPLING_SEED <- ifelse(EXECUTE_SAMPLING, round(runif(n = 1, 0, 999)), 119)

N_CHAINS <- 4
N_WARMUP <- 1000
N_SAMPLES <- 1000

# Function estimates the mode of a sample
estimate_mode <- function(x) {
  d <- density(x, n = 2^6)
  d$x[which.max(d$y)]
}
input_df <- read_csv(
  here("data", glue("{filename_stub}-sim.csv")), 
  col_types = "dddf",
  show_col_types = FALSE)

input_params <- read_tsv(
  here("data", glue("{filename_stub}-param.tsv")), 
  show_col_types = FALSE)

input_df |> 
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = t, y = y, colour = factor(d)) +
  geom_linerange(aes(ymax = y + y_se, ymin = y - y_se), colour = "black") +
  geom_point() +
  labs(colour = "Band")
input_params
# A tibble: 2 × 6
   seed     w    mu  Sigma theta   phi
  <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
1  2495 1       1.5 0.01     0       0
2  2495 0.894   1.6 0.0144   0.5     1

Model Fitting

stan_model <- cmdstan_model(here("stan", "mosmgp-D2-Q1.stan"))

Sampling

band1_df <- filter(input_df, d == 1)
band2_df <- filter(input_df, d == 2)

data_list <- list(
  N1 = length(band1_df$t),
  N2 = length(band2_df$t),
  t1 = band1_df$t,
  t2 = band2_df$t,
  y1 = band1_df$y,
  y2 = band2_df$y,
  y1_se = band1_df$y_se,
  y2_se = band2_df$y_se
)

Priors

\[w \sim \mathrm{U}[0, 10], \quad \mu \sim \mathrm{U}[0, 5], \quad \Sigma \sim \mathrm{U}[0, 5], \quad \theta_2 \sim \mathrm{U}[0, 1], \quad \phi_2 \sim \mathrm{U}[-\pi, \pi]\]

format(start_time <- Sys.time())
[1] "2026-10-20 02:21:29"
if (EXECUTE_SAMPLING) {
  init_fun <- function() {
    init =   list(
      #w = c(1, 1),
      mu = c(2.0, 2.1)
      #Sigma = c(0.9, 1.1),
      #theta2 = 0.5,
      #phi2 = 0
    )
  }

  output <- stan_model$sample(
    data = data_list,
    #init = init_fun,
    chains = N_CHAINS,
    parallel_chains = N_CHAINS,
    iter_warmup = N_WARMUP,
    iter_sampling = N_SAMPLES,
    refresh = 500,
    show_exceptions = FALSE,
    show_messages = TRUE
  )
  
  output$save_object(
    here("RDS", glue("{filename_stub}_mosmgp-D2-Q1.RDS")))
  
} else {
  output <- readRDS(
    here("RDS", glue("{filename_stub}_mosmgp-D2-Q1.RDS")))
}

format(finish_time <- Sys.time())
[1] "2026-10-20 02:21:29"
difftime(finish_time, start_time)

Posterior Predictive Check

Target locations

n_star <- 100
ts1 <- seq(from = 0, to = 10, length.out = n_star)
ts2 <- ts1
# Draw posterior predictive samples using a particular posterior draw
r <- sample.int(nrow(output_draws_mat), 1)
this_post <- output_draws_mat[r,]

pp_draw <- pred_D2_Q1_draw(this_post, t1 = band1_df$t, t2 = band2_df$t, y1 = band1_df$y, y2 = band2_df$y, y1_se = band1_df$y_se, y2_se = band2_df$y_se, ts1 = ts1, ts2 = ts2)

ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = pp_draw, aes(x = ts, y = fs, colour = d)) +
  geom_point(data = input_df, aes(x = t, y = y), size = 0.5) +
  labs(colour = "Band")
pp_draws <- pred_D2_Q1(draws = output_draws_mat, 
                       t1 = band1_df$t, 
                       t2 = band2_df$t, 
                       y1 = band1_df$y, 
                       y2 = band2_df$y, 
                       y1_se = band1_df$y_se, 
                       y2_se = band2_df$y_se, 
                       ts1 = ts1, 
                       ts2 = ts2, 
                       n_draws = 100)

ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = pp_draws, aes(x = ts, y = fs, group = interaction(d,.draw), colour = d)) +
  geom_point(data = input_df, aes(x = t, y = y), size = 1) +
  labs(colour = "Band")

output_draws |> 
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = `theta[2]`) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 40) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = diff(input_params$theta), linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = posterior_means["theta[2]"], colour = "red")

if \(\Sigma_{ij}\) is small, i.e., narrow peak in spectral domain, then the exponential envelope is broad in the time domain. This makes it difficult to distinguish \(\theta\) from \(\phi\) since both shift the oscillation. Consider using a more informative prior on \(\theta\).
